headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces off its session low with the NQ overnight range untouched for a seventh hour, as Brent tops $90 on the US strike on Iranian launchers and September Fed hike odds hold above 60%
body:
About two hours into the final August US cash session the Nasdaq-100 trades near 29,374.53, down 0.20% from a 29,433.43 previous close, inside a cash range of 29,304.49-29,465.00. The important structural detail is that the index sits roughly 70 points above its session low rather than on it: an hour ago it was pinned near 29,316 with the low at 29,306, and that low has since been retraced rather than extended. NQ futures near 29,412.25 are off 0.27% and leave the 29,274.75-29,545.50 overnight range unchanged for a seventh consecutive hourly assessment, with neither extreme retested at any point. That is the signature of two-sided price discovery, not of a persistent no-retracement trend.

The macro driver is energy and rates. Brent trades near $90.50, up 2.72%, and WTI near $85.38, up 2.37%, after US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers that were preparing to deploy mines into the Strait of Hormuz. Higher crude has fed straight into inflation expectations: traders price a better than 60% chance of a September Federal Reserve rate increase, up from about 41% a week ago after Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks. The Dallas Fed's August Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey, released at 14:30 UTC, reinforced that tone with a general business activity index of 11.6 against 1.3 in July and a production index of 16.1.

Cross-asset confirmation is partial rather than aligned, which is the main reason Tail stays low. The 10-year Treasury yield is up about 4 basis points at 4.76% while the 2-year is essentially unchanged at 4.35%, a bear steepening in which the front end stays anchored despite the hawkish repricing. VIX is up 5.06% at 15.16 within a 14.89-15.48 range, a low absolute level for a session that began with a military strike. Breadth is negative, with the Dow off about 0.64% and the Russell 2000 off about 0.86%, yet the Nasdaq-100 is the best-performing major index: Nvidia is up roughly 1% on a $3.5 billion convertible-bond investment in MediaTek tied to NVLink Fusion, and semiconductors are green. Energy names lead while utilities lag, the latter distorted by an 18% single-name decline in PG&E on wildfire liability.

Aggregating these, the pathological price path that Tail measures is not present. There is a genuine geopolitical discontinuity and a real inflation channel, but the index is mid-range, the futures range is stale, retracement is working, the front end of the curve is calm and index-level leadership is split rather than one-way. Tail is set at 12 in the low band. Stress at 52 in the elevated band reflects the unresolved oil and rate backdrop, negative breadth and month-end flow. Confidence at 87 reflects live index, futures, volatility, yield and crude readings plus a verified calendar and verified reporting; the shared Finviz cross-asset file was last collected at 07:43 UTC and is outside its 90-minute freshness bound, so it was not used as evidence. The narrow 19:00-20:15 UTC window covering the power hour and the August month-end market-on-close auction is where conditional risk concentrates. The assessment applies jointly to NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments were available and every one mapped to EA_ON. Tail held at 5 through the Sunday US afternoon and the reopen, stepped to 9 at 22:00 UTC and to 14-15 across 23:00-00:00 UTC as the Iran escalation was first priced, then decayed back to 5 by 07:00-08:00 UTC. It spiked to the window peak of 17 at 09:00 UTC as crude extended, eased through 11, 10 and 9 over the following three hours, and firmed to 12 and 13 at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC around the US cash open. Stress climbed from 27 to a peak of 53, with a dip to 47 at 12:00 UTC. Dominant mode ran normal through the Sunday session, turned mixed once the escalation was priced, showed a single trend-down hour at 00:00 UTC, ran event/whipsaw at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC on the crude spike, and has been mixed for the last four hours. No hour in the window reached the watch band.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps the mapped state at EA_ON for all 24 hours, with conditional Tail never leaving the low band. It runs 12 in the current hour, holds 11-12 through the European close and the quiet US midday, then rises to 15 and a horizon peak of 16 for the 19:00 and 20:00 UTC month-end rebalancing and cash-close pair, the only two slots carried as event/whipsaw on 31 August. It falls to 11 after the close and settles to an 8-9 overnight floor across the Asian session, where five hours are carried as normal. From the European pre-open it rebuilds gradually through 10-11, steps to 12-13 as US pre-market flow builds, and reaches 14 at the 1 September cash open and 16 for the 14:00 UTC hour carrying ISM Manufacturing, JOLTS and construction spending. Conditional Stress tracks the same shape between a 33 floor overnight and 56 at the two peaks, while Confidence decays from 87 to 62 across the horizon as observed evidence gives way to scheduled-catalyst inference.
